content.comment_body: Hello! I ordered some [product_name] modules with manufacturing date 07.2018, firmware version [version_no]. The box indicates FS:01, while I expected FS:04 or higher, since FS:04 was already available in 2016. I purchased these because I needed Modbus support. Could it be that this is a newer product generation and the FS numbers have restarted from 01, meaning this module is newer than FS:04?

The module you have is the most recent [product_name], which is newer than previous hardware versions (FS04-FS06). It has been available since December 2017. For more details, refer to the delivery release information for [product_name] [version_no].

Thanks for clarifying! Can you point out where exactly the box lists the version? Does [version_no] refer to [product_name] software version? The packaging mentions '[version_no] or later required', so it's unlikely the version ties directly to the firmware. Or is the '82' in the firmware number referencing the version? I suppose I overlooked differences between article numbers. These details can certainly be confusing. Thanks again!

It's actually more complex. The new [product_name] [version_no] hardware corresponds to an earlier hardware revision, but features updated firmware. Because it shares hardware specifications with previous revisions, using [product_name] software [version_no] is sufficient unless you need newer features available in [product_name] software [version_no]. In device selection, both software versions list the same hardware revision. Upgrade the software only if you want access to newer functionalities.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing confusion regarding [company_name] hardware and firmware versioning for [product_name]. There's uncertainty as to why a new module is labeled with an older revision number (FS:01), despite the existence of higher revisions required for specific support like Modbus. The connection between firmware, hardware numbers, and compatible software versions is unclear, and documentation does not adequately clarify this, leaving users unsure about device capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear product labeling and versioning on packaging to identify feature support such as Modbus. They also seek precise documentation that explains the relationships between hardware revisions, firmware versions, and compatible software versions, enabling straightforward determination of the module's capabilities.
